fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Teeth that are cracked, heavily filled or badly worn can become fragile and uncomfortable. Missing teeth can affect how you chew, how your remaining teeth are positioned and how you feel when you smile. Dental crowns and bridges are fixed restorations that help protect weakened teeth and replace missing ones.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we explain every suitable option, including when a smaller restoration or an alternative such as an implant may be more appropriate.

sections.label: What Are Dental Crowns and Bridges?

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Dental Crowns and Bridges?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A dental crown is a custom-made cap that covers the entire visible part of a tooth. It restores the tooth's shape and strength and helps protect it from further damage. Crowns can be made from ceramic, porcelain fused to metal, zirconia or gold, depending on the tooth and your needs.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A dental bridge replaces one or more missing teeth. It typically consists of an artificial tooth held in place by crowns on the neighbouring teeth, or on dental implants. Once fitted, a bridge is fixed in place and is not removed for cleaning.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Are Crowns and Bridges Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A crown may be recommended if you have:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A tooth with a large filling and little remaining structure

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A cracked or fractured tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A tooth that has had root canal therapy

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Severely worn or discoloured teeth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A bridge may be considered if you have one or more missing teeth and healthy neighbouring teeth or implants to support it. Because a traditional bridge involves shaping the adjacent teeth, we will also discuss alternatives such as dental implants and dentures, along with the benefits and limitations of each.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Assessment and Planning

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine your teeth, take digital X-rays and check your bite and gum health. We explain our findings, outline your options and provide a written quote.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Preparation

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Using local anaesthetic, the tooth or teeth are carefully shaped to make space for the restoration. A digital scan records the prepared teeth in detail.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Your Restoration

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many single crowns can be designed and milled in our practice using CEREC, allowing same-day fitting. Other crowns and most bridges are made by a dental laboratory, in which case a temporary restoration is placed while you wait.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Fitting

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We check the fit, appearance and bite of your restoration, make any refinements, and cement or bond it securely in place.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Brush twice daily and clean between your teeth each day. For bridges, floss threaders, interdental brushes or a water flosser help clean beneath the replacement tooth. Avoid chewing very hard objects, and wear a night splint if you grind. Regular check-ups and cleans allow us to monitor the edges of your restorations and the health of your gums.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Crowns and Bridges

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Crowns and Bridges

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We combine careful diagnosis with digital scanning and in-house CEREC technology, which means many single crowns can be completed in one visit. Dr Billy Choi takes time to explain every option, so you understand why a crown or bridge is recommended and what alternatives are available.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How long do crowns and bridges last?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Their lifespan varies depending on the material, your oral hygiene, your bite and grinding habits. With good care and regular reviews, many restorations serve well for years, but they may eventually need replacement.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Does getting a crown hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Local anaesthetic keeps you comfortable during preparation. Some tenderness or sensitivity afterwards is common and usually settles within a few days.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What is the difference between a bridge and an implant?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A bridge is supported by neighbouring teeth or implants, while an implant replaces the tooth root on its own. Each has benefits and limitations, which we discuss at your consultation.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I get a crown in one visit?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many single crowns can be made in one visit using our CEREC system. Bridges and some crowns require a dental laboratory and a second appointment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will a crown look like my other teeth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We select the material and shade to suit your tooth and surrounding teeth. You can review the colour before your restoration is fitted.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can a crowned tooth still get decay?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. Decay can develop where the crown meets the natural tooth, so brushing, cleaning between teeth and regular check-ups remain important.
